purpose: Famciclovir is used to treat infections caused by certain viruses, including shingles (herpes zoster), cold sores, and genital herpes. It can help reduce pain, speed up healing of sores, and shorten how long the outbreak lasts. It can also be used regularly to help prevent herpes outbreaks from coming back.
how_it_works: Famciclovir works by blocking the virus from making copies of itself inside your body. Once you take it, your body converts it into an active form that targets the virus directly. This slows the spread of the virus so your immune system can do a better job fighting the infection.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include headache, nausea, diarrhea, and dizziness. Some people may also notice tiredness or stomach pain. Most of these are mild and go away on their own as your body adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have kidney problems, because the dose may need to be adjusted for you. Famciclovir does not cure herpes — it only helps control it, and you can still pass the virus to others even while taking it. Avoid sexual contact during outbreaks, and always use protection. Contact your doctor right away if you notice confusion, unusual bruising or bleeding, or signs of an allergic reaction like rash, swelling, or trouble breathing.
typical_dosing: The dose depends on what condition is being treated. For shingles, a common dose is 500 mg taken three times a day for 7 days. For genital herpes outbreaks, it may be 1000 mg twice a day for just one day. For prevention of recurring herpes, a typical dose is 250 mg twice a day. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes and try to start it as soon as possible after symptoms begin.
